name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 18 points
Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage ($7.4M raised)
Open seat after Jasmine Crockett's retirement to run for Senate
Prediction markets price Democrats near 96% to hold the seat
model.rationale: The seat's 18-point Democratic lean, Allred's heavy fundraising edge, and markets pricing Democrats around 96% all point to a safe hold despite the open seat. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals with a modest haircut for open-seat uncertainty.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Gillespie or an unusually low-turnout special dynamic could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Dallas-area House seat is strongly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 18 points, and Democrats have held it comfortably. Jasmine Crockett is leaving to run for Senate, so the seat is open, but the Democratic nominee, Colin Allred, is a well-known former Senate candidate who has raised more than $7.4 million. His Republican opponent, Patrick Gillespie, reports little fundraising activity.

Prediction markets price Democrats at roughly 96% to hold the seat, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The main uncertainty is typical open-seat variability rather than genuine two-party competition. All signs point to a comfortable Democratic hold in November.
